national.title: Zelenskyy says Ukrainian drone attack hit Russian warship at naval base in Libya
national.summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.
national.body:
In this satellite image provided by Vantor, the capsized Russian navy corvette Merkury is seen following a suspected drone strike, at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Satellite image ©2026 Vantor/via AP hide caption

KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made sea drones in the operation, which struck a Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 invasion of its neighbor, the Ukrainian leader said in a post on X.

The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spiderweb in June last year when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked near air bases across Russia.

Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."

"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.

Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that a Ka-27 military helicopter was destroyed in the attack.

national.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
national.summary: Older drivers are using Tesla's automated driving technology to stay on the road longer. But safety experts warn the company may be over-selling what its cars can do.
national.body:
Joan Spalding, 89, sits behind the wheel of her Tesla Model Y, equipped with Full-Self Driving (Supervised) technology, on a recent drive near her home in Evergreen, Colo. Jimena Peck for NPR hide caption

EVERGREEN, Colo. — Joan Spalding has driven the steep, winding road that leads to her house outside Denver for more than 50 years. But these days, the 89-year-old barely touches the steering wheel or the pedals.

Instead she tells the car where she wants to go, and presses a button on the large touch-screen in the dashboard of her Tesla Model Y.

For all practical purposes, the car appears to be driving itself, navigating confidently on twisting roads through postcard valleys full of juniper and ponderosa pine.

"Now this is probably one of the narrowest roads," Spalding says, as the car pulls onto a dirt track that can barely fit two cars side by side, with a steep drop off to one side.

The Tesla handles the tight turns gracefully, even stopping to let an SUV squeeze by in the other lane.

Spalding was skeptical at first of what Tesla officially calls Full-Self Driving (Supervised), often abbreviated as FSD. It's a subscription service that drivers pay for, usually $99 dollars per month.

"When I was driving," Spalding said, "I saw that the kind of things that it did were safer than what I would do."

national.title: When disaster strikes, Medicaid work rules add barriers
national.summary: Medicaid provides a critical safety net for people to maintain healthcare coverage. But new work requirements create barriers for those trying to recover from natural disasters.
national.body: PO'IPŪ, Hawai'i — A month after Hurricane Lowell hit the island of Kauaʻi, downed trees, construction crews, and damaged homes dotted the neighborhoods. At the Sheraton Kauaʻi Resort, where over 100 workers were laid off, heaps of sand blanketed the grounds, and the drained pool's concrete deck crumbled into the beach, just steps away from the ocean.On Kauaʻi, unemployment claims jumped from 69 before the September hurricane to about 1,800 nearly two weeks afterward, with widespread layoffs in the tourism industry amid a sharp decline in visitors. The number of Medicaid applications submitted by island residents jumped by about 50% in the following month, according to the Hawaiʻi Department of Human Services.In times of emergencies, Medicaid provides a critical safety net for people to maintain healthcare coverage. But new work rules in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which President Trump signed last year, has put Medicaid enrollees living in disaster-struck counties at risk of losing health insurance. The law requires many nondisabled adults enrolled in Medicaid in 43 states and Washington, D.C., to work, volunteer, or attend school at least 80 hours a month, with eligibility checks starting in January.In most states, residents impacted by a disaster can be granted a short-term exemption from Medicaid work requirements. Eligibility largely relies on a federal law that allows the president to issue a disaster or emergency declaration and authorizes federal assistance, but any declaration can take months or may not come at all.Those who live in counties affected by natural disasters may not need to comply with the work rules — one of several carve-outs intended to provide limited, short-term exceptions. However, it's unclear whether those who lost jobs after Hurricane Lowell would be eligible for that exemption so many months later. The Trump administration hasn't offered clear guidance on how long a state can apply the natural disaster exemption to enrollees.Rochelle Ganotisi, a mother of five, and her boyfriend were laid off by Sheraton and are getting by with unemployment payments and part-time work. national.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to restore ties after tensions over conflict
national.summary: The two leaders committed to upholding sovereignty and "non-interference in the internal affairs of states".
national.body:
Kenya's President William Ruto and his Congolese counterpart Felix Tshisekedi have agreed to restore full diplomatic ties between the two countries following tensions over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

Relations between the two countries have soured since 2023 when DR Congo accused Kenya of hosting leaders launching a rebel alliance, including the M23.

This led DR Congo to recall its envoy to Nairobi. Relations deteriorated further when Kinshasa refusing to accredit Kenya's nominated ambassador.

On Sunday, the two leaders affirmed their commitment to "sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference in the internal affairs of states".

The agreement was announced in a joint statement issued after the summit held in the town of Oyo in Congo-Brazzaville, facilitated by the nation's President Denis Sassou Nguesso, with Togolese leader Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé as mediator.

Tshisekedi and Ruto also agreed to "good neighbourliness and peaceful settlement of disputes" as well as "strengthen cooperation within regional mechanisms".

DR Congo and Kenya are both members of the East African Community (EAC).

DR Congo, which joined in 2022, is the latest entrant to the bloc, but its membership has been complicated by its accusation that Rwanda, a fellow member, backs the M23 rebels. Rwanda denies the claims despite overwhelming evidence.

national.title: Burnham to tell MPs 'landmark' EU deal could make next decade 'much better'
national.summary: The prime minister will tell MPs the deal agreed on Friday is a "choice between a broken status quo or change".
national.body:
The prime minister will tell Parliament on Monday the "landmark" deal struck with the EU means there is a "very real prospect" the next decade can be "much better" than the last one.

The deal, which covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme , is a "choice between a broken status quo or change", Andy Burnham will tell MPs.

He will also call it "the single biggest growth measure to be delivered in this parliament" - repeating his claim it could add £17bn to the British economy.

But opposition parties have criticised the plan, with the Conservatives branding it unfair as UK farmers would have to follow rules made by Brussels.

The agreements announced on Friday included scrapping most of the checks on British food exports, in return for the UK following some EU regulations, from 2028.

Meanwhile, the new youth experience scheme , which is due to launch no later than January 2030, will allow up to 100,000 18 to 31-year-olds from the EU to travel, work and study in the UK for up to three years. The same number of young Britons will be allowed into Europe.

Burnham believes the agreement reached in Brussels "holds out the very real prospect that the next decade can be a much better one for Britain than the one we have just lived through".

"The ability to draw a line on a decade of drift and division is in our hands and I believe we should take it," he will say in his speech.

national.title: Russian ships hit by Ukrainian drones off Libya coast, Zelensky says
national.summary: Libya's eastern government says a sunken warship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.
national.body:
A Russian warship was sunk by Ukrainian drones off the coast of Libya on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

The attack also hit a second Russian vessel, a cargo ship being used to transport weapons, the Ukrainian prime minister claimed.

On Sunday morning, the government that controls eastern Libya said there had been an explosion on the warship at the Benghazi port, while it was docking for fuel and supplies ahead of its return to Russia.

Meanwhile, the health ministry said it had received injured people from a commercial ship that was targeted off the coast of the port. It is not clear whether this is the same vessel as the one Ukraine has claimed responsibility for.

In a statement on Monday, Zelensky praised an "exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia's war".

Seven naval drones were deployed to target and sink the corvette Merkury, one of Russia's newest ships, Zelensky wrote. He added that a Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed.

The Ukrainian president said the second ship was the MV ANGARA, a Russian container carrier.

The attack came the day after a Russian cargo vessel was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland . The Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning.

national.title: Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31
national.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya was the longest-running climate talks in UN history.
national.body:
The COP31 summit in Turkey came as evidence of climate change could not have been clearer - 2026 bought glacier collapses, record European heat, and wildfires across Asia - but also when geopolitical divisions could not have been deeper.

The result was the longest-running climate talks in UN history failed to deliver on its central political agreement – the Antalya Pacts - to further climate action.

Despite two countries, Australia and Turkey, leading the charge in their joint hosting of the negotiations, they could not bring the nations together.

After a dramatic and fractious final day where countries walked out over the absence of mention of fossil fuels in the text and money issues, questions are being asked more loudly than ever before about whether the COP process can still deliver.

national.title: What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks?
national.summary: The talks have been the longest-running in the summit's history, with negotiations breaking down two days after they had been due to end.
national.body:
What's next after no deal at COP31 climate talks? Close The COP31 climate summit in Turkey has officially come to an end after countries failed to come to a consensus on a new deal.

The European Union and some other countries rejected a fourth draft agreement over its failure to mention a need to phase out fossil fuels, the largest driver of global climate change.

Two days of additional negotiations made it the longest talks in the summit's history.

The failure to reach a deal triggered criticism from prominent climate advocates, including former US Vice President Al Gore, who wrote it was "outrageous that a handful of petro-states have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels".

BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard reports from Antalya, in Turkey.

national.title: Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble hours after Russian strike on Ukraine, rescuers say
national.summary: Eleven people are dead in the attack on Dymer, with rescue efforts ongoing to find those still missing from the residential building.
national.body:
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after 14 hours. Overnight Russian strikes on the village killed 11 people, Ukrainian officials have said.

The attack occurred in the early hours of Sunday. A 79-year-old woman was also rescued alive from the collapsed building, Kyiv's regional head Tymur Tkachenko said.

A strike on a private home in Bila Tserkva killed one more person and set the building ablaze, he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also said three people were killed and 13 wounded in a separate strike on Vyshneve, also in the Kyiv region, that hit a grocery store on Sunday.

Ukrainian authorities said the boy in Dymer is in stable condition and was taken to hospital, and have thanked everyone involved in saving his life.

Zelensky and Ukraine's national police also confirmed the rescue of the boy.

In a Telegram post, Tkachenko said the 79-year-old woman rescued from the rubble was receiving treatment in hospital.

Earlier he said six people were injured in the attack, while others were still missing.

national.title: Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed
national.summary: The prime minister of Australia, which co-hosted COP31, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".
national.body:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.

Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.

But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.

The last time a COP's main political agreement collapsed like this was in 2009 in Copenhagen.

UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, in his last COP before he steps down, said he was "deeply disappointed".

He took aim at what he called "powerful fossil fuel interests" who he said were taking "a page from Big Tobacco's playbook: distorting the science, delaying policy, blocking action, and piling up huge profits while people everywhere pay the price".

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, whose country co-hosted the talks, attributed the failure to "difficult geopolitical times".

national.summary: Tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and ESPN analyst, has died at 75.
national.body: Former football star and famed broadcaster Tom Jackson has died, his family and ESPN announced Sunday. Jackson rose to prominence as a Denver Broncos player and went on to build a career as a beloved NFL analyst for ESPN, becoming a mainstay of the network's Sunday football programs for three decades, including its "Sunday NFL Countdown" show. He was 75.Jimmy Pitaro, the chairman of ESPN, praised Jackson in a statement released by the network after his death. In it, Pitaro called Jackson "one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN's history," who "brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans.""Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends," Pitaro said. "Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure."Jackson's family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wish that his death not be announced until the start of the network's "Sunday NFL Countdown" show by Jackson's longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman."Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom's was frequent and unmistakable," Berman said at the start of the show. "Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. national.title: Seattle airport operator 'outraged' over ICE arrest of two passengers
national.summary: ICE said a man and a woman, both Mexican nationals, were arrested for allegedly overstaying their visas.
national.body:
US immigration authorities faced criticism after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arrested two passengers as they were boarding a flight in Seattle.

The incident happened on Saturday morning local time at the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), when ICE said a man and a woman, both Mexican nationals, were arrested for allegedly overstaying their visas.

It said that, during its arrest of the man - named as Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza - "other travellers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers", which it described as a "federal crime and a felony".

The Port said in a statement that it was "outraged" about the incident.

Alaska Airlines said the incident happened during the boarding of one of its flights to Los Angeles and that it was not given "appropriate notice of the enforcement action".

It also said it was "concerned" about the arrests and recognised "how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests".

Both the airline and the Port of Seattle, which owns and runs the airport, said they were looking into whether the proper protocols were followed.

The Port said: "Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port's participation or knowledge."

national.title: U.N. climate summit ends without deal after contentious fossil fuel debate
national.summary: COP31, the latest installment of the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed.
national.body: COP31, the United Nations' annual climate conference, ended Sunday without a final agreement after days of contentious talks collapsed, mainly because of disputes between nations pushing to phase out fossil fuel use and others opposed to doing so.The breakdown capped two weeks of negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, between delegations from nearly 200 countries. Their debates ran into overtime, becoming the longest COP summit in history, at a moment that U.N. officials and many scientists have called decisive for the trajectory of global warming and climate change.U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres said in a statement that Sunday he was "deeply disappointed" by the outcome of the summit."I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," he said. "But this setback does not change the facts. There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science."The United States sent no representatives to the climate conference for the second year in a row, following the Trump administration's withdrawal from the 2015 Paris Agreement. That accord set a goal of limiting warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, a target that has anchored every U.N. climate summit since and that the world is now poised to overshoot.Talks reached an impasse Sunday, as the European Union opposed a draft agreement that failed to mention fossil fuels and which, its delegates argued, placated countries that export them. "We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuel, which is the key driver of climate change," said Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for the EU in Antalya. national.summary: Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday
national.body: Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday, federal officials said, causing what Alaska Airlines called a "distressing" scene for passengers and employees and delaying the Los Angeles-bound flight.Videos of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as a woman screamed that her daughter was being taken and she has a work permit. Alaska Airlines said U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday."We are concerned by this morning's law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306," the airline said. "We recognize how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests."An Alaska Airlines spokesperson told CBS News on Sunday that the flight, scheduled to depart at 8:45 a.m., left the airport at 11:03 a.m. after some crew members asked to leave."Immediately following the incident, some inflight crew members requested to be replaced. As we learned more about what occurred, we ultimately brought in an entirely new crew," the airline spokesperson said in a statement.In a statement provided to CBS News Saturday evening, a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, the parent agency of ICE, said that ICE officers "conducted a targeted enforcement operation" on a Mexican national identified as Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza who had "overstayed his visa."During the arrest, a second passenger "hurled hot coffee" at the officers, the DHS spokesperson said in the statement. national.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
national.summary: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.
national.body:
Fiona, a Nile Hippopotamus, eats her specialty birthday cake to celebrate turning three-years old this Friday, in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, Thursday, Jan. 23, 2020, in Cincinnati. John Minchillo/AP hide caption

The death of Fiona, a beloved hippopotamus who captured hearts, has renewed calls to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.

Fiona, 9 years old, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat at the Cincinnati Zoo. The zoo said that the hat was lodged in the hippo's small intestine and surgery was not possible.

"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement .

While deaths are rare, items such as coins, shoes and sunglasses frequently fall, and sometimes are tossed, into animal enclosures.

In 2024, 70 U.S. coins were successfully removed from an alligator at Omaha's Henry Doorly Zoo and Aquarium. And in 2025, a Komodo dragon ate a shoe that was thrown into its habitat at the Memphis Zoo. The shoe was removed and the dragon survived.

Dr. Gabriella Flacke, an associate veterinarian at Zoo Miami, said the zoo's staff have retrieved items such as cellphones from alligators.

"We've had to remove those items both endoscopically, which is basically putting a camera through the mouth and down into the stomach to grab and retrieve those items, or we've in a few cases had to do surgery where they were larger items that couldn't be removed that way," Flacke told NPR.

national.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
national.summary: Democrats have now won at least 258 seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats.
national.body:
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.

The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.

Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.

Sunday's result came after Foxx, who has represented North Carolina's 5th Congressional District since 2005, requested a recount. This is allowed under state law when the margin of victory is under 1%.

"I think the American people are just sick of what's going on and they wanted a change. They voted for change," Hubbard told the BBC News Channel after his victory. He pledged to work alongside his fellow lawmakers to hold President Donald Trump accountable.

Earlier, he wrote on X that he had spoken to Foxx, "who graciously conceded following the results of the recount process".

Hubbard added: "I deeply appreciate her commitment to a smooth transition of the office and constituent casework. We may not always agree, but we both love North Carolina and the people of the Fifth District."

national.body: For most of the year, Kevin "Country" Gildhouse and Travis "Buckethead" Johnson are prison inmates serving a life sentence without parole. But sometimes, they don cowboy hats and spurs for a rodeo dubbed "the wildest show in the South"Through good behavior, around 1,000 incarcerated men at Louisiana State Penitentiary, the largest maximum security prison in the country, earn the right to several privileges, including the option to participate in the Angola Prison Rodeo. Outside the prison walls, the rodeo has elicited charges of exploitation. But inside, the incarcerated men say it's a chance at a fleeting moment of freedom during their life sentences."You're free. You're not in prison. You're just out here competing"Gildhouse remembers being scared to death when he was taken to the Louisiana State Penitentiary nearly two decades ago. "I'm about to go to the place they say I'm gonna die in," he said. Gildhouse grew up in what he described as a broken family. He was in foster care and "bounced through probably about 72 homes throughout my childhood."At 19, he was sentenced to life without parole after he was convicted of killing a cab driver in a botched robbery. To this day, Gildhouse thinks about the man he killed, and while he feels he could never ask for forgiveness from the man's family, he does believe he's been forgiven by God. national.summary: 60 Minutes goes inside a growing, online community of young people who idolize, romanticize and sometimes even seek to emulate mass shooters.
national.body: The True Crime Community, known as the TCC by its members, is a growing online community of young people who idolize and romanticize mass shooters.Allizandra Herberhold is a licensed social worker who's spent two years undercover on social media platforms studying the TCC and its members. Herberhold is what's called a "deradicalizer" and has helped 18 kids leave the TCC. She says most kids age out of the dark interest in violence, but some need extra help."Because I don't speak about them like they're monsters," she said. "I see them as children who are struggling, and they need help."Here are five takeaways from 60 Minutes' report on TCC:TCC is a growing, online subculture Herberhold said most kids inside the TCC are desperate for community, outsiders who are often bullied at school, isolated, and dealing with trouble at home. Because the substances are so new, when they first emerge in the U.S. drug supply, they are technically legal. Eventually, regulation catches up, the substance is made illegal, and the drug cartels move on and create other drugs. national.summary: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".
national.body:
Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89.

His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media.

Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales.

The company Bvlgari posted an online tribute to the "true creative soul", whose work would "continue to inspire generations to come".

The firm, Bulgari, was set up by his grandfather, Greek silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris, in Rome in the late 19th century - who later adapted his name to Bulgari in Italian.

Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewellery, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome.

Paolo Bulgari joined the company shortly after leaving school, becoming an expert in gemstones - eventually leading the business and overseeing international growth.

The Bulgari family favoured bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions and unexpected colour combinations to set them apart from the delicate asethetic associated with Parisian jewellery houses.

national.title: In their own words: Leaders at UN climate talks discuss why negotiations ended without deal
national.summary: After reviewing a draft of the agreement released by co-host Turkey, a number of countries spoke up during the final meeting Sunday to say they couldn't accept a deal that failed to include wording on fossil fuels.
national.body:
Suzan Fraser, Associated Press Suzan Fraser, Associated Press

Anton L. Delgado, Associated Press Anton L. Delgado, Associated Press

ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — The words of negotiators and other leaders at the U.N. climate talks illustrate why the meeting failed to reach a final agreement.

Each year the annual meeting seeks to hammer out a document known as a cover decision that gives direction on how countries around the world should fight climate change. But at the meetings in Turkey this time, negotiators could not overcome impasses on whether the final document should mention fossil fuels. The burning of fuels such as coal, oil and gas is what causes global warming.

After reviewing a draft of the agreement released by co-host Turkey, a number of countries spoke up during the final meeting Sunday to say they couldn't accept a deal that failed to include wording on fossil fuels. Others spoke to reporters on the sidelines of the plenary sessions. The co-hosts Turkey and Australia also offered their thoughts.

Below are the views of the players at COP31, in their own words.

"I want to clearly state that the European Union and its member states object to this cover decision in both its iterations, and that we're saying that on behalf of our citizens, our member states, because these decisions go nowhere near the level of action or ambition that are required for us to tackle climate change, it is unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel."

"Our responsibility is not to negotiate the minimum threshold, our responsibility is to do what is right. Our responsibility is to protect the planet. ... This is an issue of justice. President, please allow us to explain briefly why Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed to commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it (relies) too much upon technologies such as, CCS capture storage of carbon, instead of calling for deep changes. And, three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback."

national.summary: Earlier Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta's hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.
national.body:
Jamie Stengle, Associated Press Jamie Stengle, Associated Press

Well over half of Delta Air Lines flights were experiencing delays Sunday afternoon following a problem with an automation system during a busy time for travel ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

The airline said its teams were using manual workarounds to get flights off the ground while they continued to work to restore automation of a system that calculates weight to ensure an aircraft isn't too heavy to fly. Hours later, Delta said that system was once again working, though flights were still not back to normal. About 1,000 of the airline's flights were delayed as of Sunday afternoon.

Earlier Sunday, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta's hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.

Complying with the weight and balance limits of an aircraft is critical to flight safety, according to an FAA document, and going above the limit can compromise the structural integrity of the aircraft.

The agency said on X that the delays weren't related to FAA air traffic systems.

Earlier this month, a malfunction in the FAA's network led to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years. The stop lasted for more than four hours, and carriers canceled and delayed swaths of flights as they worked to recover. Just days after that, United Airlines saw its own system outage — forcing it to delay departing flights.

The Delta delays come as Americans have been encountering a growing number of problems with technology that are increasingly disrupting their lives.

local.summary: December 15 marks the official voting day that eligible residents in the Clymer, Sherman and Panama school districts will be deciding whether or not to move forward and merge the three school districts into one. A feasibility study that has been done on the potential merger includes the details behi
local.body:
December 15 marks the official voting day that eligible residents in the Clymer, Sherman and Panama school districts will be deciding whether or not to move forward and merge the three school districts into one.

A feasibility study that has been done on the potential merger includes the details behind the decision to look into this merger, including why the three communities are considering a change and how this change could affect the students in these three districts. One of the most major reasons behind looking into this merger is the decline in enrollment in all three districts.

CSP Merger Study Project Coordinator, Shelly O'Boyle, shared that over the last 30 years student enrollment across the three districts has dropped by 52 percent, as outlined in the merger feasibility study. This percentage means that enrollment across all three districts has fallen from 2,169 students in 1995 to 1,041 in 2025. Today, Clymer, Panama and Sherman have three of the five smallest student populations out of all 18 school districts in Chautauqua County.

The feasibility study projects that with a combined district there will be between 920 and 980 students total by 2030. As individual grades shrink, O'Boyle said that some classes are projected to have fewer than 15 students and it becomes much harder for each district to afford specialized teachers, classes and buildings on their own.

"While shrinking enrollment is one of the main reasons for exploring a merger, the study shows that combining resources could create new opportunities for students, which local residents ranked as their top priority," O'Boyle said. "All three districts already have strong graduation rates. Merging at the high school level would allow students to share a combined 60 electives and 29 college-level courses through Jamestown Community College and Hilbert College without small class sizes getting in the way."

Outside the classroom, the three districts have already successfully shared multiple CSP sports teams. O'Boyle said a formal merger is set to make those teams more sustainable, open the door to new sports, and bring together 21 clubs, music and arts programs.

"For special education, the study recommends that a merged district would form a new committee made up of staff from all three communities," O'Boyle said. "This approach would keep student support familiar while offering more special education services in-house."

On Nov. 10, Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders released a new book entitled, “Unapologetic: Clarity and Conviction in a World Gone Crazy.”

Unlike most midterm Republican candidates, Sanders won reelection in a landslide.

I had the opportunity to hear her speak about her new book at the Nixon Library on Veterans Day and was so inspired that I, like others in the room, wondered out loud if she should be on the GOP short list for presidential nominee in 2028.

Her newest book, “Unapologetic,” tracks her journey serving as press secretary in the White House to becoming the first woman elected governor of Arkansas. It gets really personal as she shares the fear she overcame in her battle with cancer that was diagnosed just 60 days before her first election — and the faith that sustained her then and continues to guide her every day.

As she first ran for governor, Sanders addressed issues that she believes matter most to Arkansans: education, lower taxes, jobs and public safety. And she delivered as a conservative on those issues and was unapologetically pro-life.

Sanders was reelected by a 15-point margin in an election cycle where Republicans suffered crushing losses all across America, including in her neighboring state of Texas.

Every Republican state official on the ballot was elected, along with the entire Arkansas Republican congressional delegation.

While she has supported many of President Donald Trump’s policy positions, Sarah expresses a nuanced view on the issue of artificial intelligence. She supports guardrails around AI and opposed a provision in the original version of the One Big Beautiful Bill that would have prevented states from regulating AI. That provision was stripped following objections by her and only a handful of other Republicans.

local.title: The OBSERVER’s View: Safety net spending problem has many causes
local.summary: The Chautauqua County Legislature doesn’t have much choice but to pay the ever-escalating bill for safety net spending – but that doesn’t mean the county has to handle this expense the same way it has over the past few years, either. In October county lawmakers approved a resolution that moves $2,13
local.body:
The Chautauqua County Legislature doesn’t have much choice but to pay the ever-escalating bill for safety net spending - but that doesn’t mean the county has to handle this expense the same way it has over the past few years, either.

In October county lawmakers approved a resolution that moves $2,130,000 from its unassigned fund balance to the Safety Net account to pay the county’s share of costs for single adults; childless couples; children living with a caretaker other than a parent; families of persons abusing drugs or alcohol; families of persons refusing drug alcohol screening, assessment, or treatment; people who have exceeded the 60-month limit on assistance; and non-citizens who are eligible for temporary assistance, but who are not eligible for federal reimbursement. The good news is that the $2.13 million is less than the $2.8 million the county Department of Social Services had requested earlier in the year to cover the shortfall. The bad news is that the drop county officials saw in June that prompted the earlier request to be rescinded wasn’t sustainable.

In fact, if there’s one thing the county can take to the bank next year, it’s that safety net spending will exceed what the county has budgeted. We’d still like to see the safety net budget increased in the budget each year so that mid-year adjustments aren’t needed. In our opinion, that number is at least $16 million in 2027, if not closer to $16.5 million. Doing so would mean county residents have a more clear understanding how much safety net programs are costing each year and avoids the mid-year budget adjustment.

It’s nice to have the surplus to make up the difference between budget spending for safety net program costs and what is actually spent, but it is preferable to actually set the budget high enough that the yearly budget adjustment isn’t needed.

Just as importantly, we aren’t sure why the county didn’t just allocate more money this summer. We hope it’s not to avoid Legislator Fred Johnson’s push to reduce other departments’ budgets to pay for safety net program spending needs. We agree with Johnson, finding the money in the approved budget is preferable to simply taking from the county surplus. But it is a lot more work for county department heads, and given the slight difference between the June and October DSS spending requests, we wonder if the delay in appropriating the money was to make the increased spending take place later in the year so Johnson and those who agree with his line of thinking would have no choice but to use the surplus to pay the increased cost.

local.summary: SINCLAIRVILLE — A proposed $18.2 million capital improvement project at Cassadaga Valley Central School is set to have no additional tax impact for members of the school district. local.body:
SINCLAIRVILLE -- A proposed $18.2 million capital improvement project at Cassadaga Valley Central School is set to have no additional tax impact for members of the school district.

This planned project has been in the works for a while, with planning beginning in the 2024-2025 school year. Superintendent Tammy Mangus noted that caring for the district's schools is ongoing work and that the district has a long history of using the Building Conditions Survey, mandated for every five years, to identify the buildings' core needs. This is followed by the creation of capital outlays and capital improvement projects to ensure that the district's buildings maintain their "breathtaking beauty while evaluating and addressing building condition needs and student needs."

"This proposal brings those pieces together: taking care of aging facilities, improving spaces for students, and planning the financial commitment so we can sustain it," Mangus said. "The proposed $18.2 million project addresses needs at Sinclairville Elementary School, the Middle-High School, and our Bus Garage."

The project at Sinclairville Elementary includes replacing outdated classroom heating and ventilation equipment, adding cafeteria cooling, upgrading the water distribution systems, replacing deteriorated flooring and addressing the kitchen cooler and related structural needs. At the Middle-High School, the work includes heating and cooling improvements, including cooling for the gym and third floor; water distribution upgrades; classroom flooring; and improvements to the Cougar Café and cafeteria. It also includes converting the middle school locker rooms into student service suites and an updated health office. At the Bus Garage, the proposal includes heating and ventilation improvements in the bus bays and roof replacement.

"If voters approve the project in December, the anticipated schedule includes design in 2027, New York State Education Department review in 2028, and construction from approximately 2029 through 2031," Mangus said. "That timeline also helps explain why planning ahead matters. These projects take time to move from identifying a need to completing the work."

Mangus said this capital improvement project is important because education provides students with opportunities, and the places where students learn need to be able to support those opportunities on a daily basis. This means having dependable heat, appropriate ventilation, functioning water systems, sound roofs, and spaces where students can receive the care and support they need.

local.summary: Tom Jackson, a fiery cornerstone of the Orange Crush defense with the Denver Broncos who went on to even more fame as a beloved broadcaster on ESPN, has died, his family and the network announced Sunday. He was 75. Jackson’s family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wishes that his
local.body:
Tom Jackson, a fiery cornerstone of the Orange Crush defense with the Denver Broncos who went on to even more fame as a beloved broadcaster on ESPN, has died, his family and the network announced Sunday. He was 75.

Jackson’s family informed ESPN that he died Friday, but it was their wishes that his death not be announced until the start of the network’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” show by Jackson’s longtime friend and on-air partner Chris Berman. A cause of death was not given.

“Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst. There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable,” Berman said. “Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend, too.”

Berman said Jackson made a surprise visit a couple of weeks ago to ESPN, where he worked for 32 years over two stints after playing 14 seasons for the Broncos, and that the two talked on Tuesday.

A fourth-round draft pick out of Louisville in 1973, Jackson was an inspirational leader of Denver’s first Super Bowl team in 1977. He started 177 games for the Broncos between 1973-86, retiring after the team’s second Super Bowl appearance. He was a first-team All-Pro in 1977 and a second-team All-Pro the following season; he also was a three-time Pro Bowler.

The Broncos held a moment of silence and showed a video tribute to Jackson prior to their game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.

Following his playing days, Jackson had a second career at ESPN from 1987-2016 and was featured on “Sunday NFL Countdown” and “NFL Primetime.”

Before the internet, and before NBC took over the Sunday night package in 2006, “NFL Primetime” was must-see viewing for fans and players because it showed highlights from all the games, as well as the interaction between Berman and Jackson, who often finished each other’s sentences.

local.summary: Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason’s market, has agreed to a record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday. The person spoke on condition of anonym
local.body:
Tarik Skubal, the two-time Cy Young Award winner who was the top free agent on this offseason’s market, has agreed to a record $450 million, nine-year contract with the New York Mets, a person familiar with the negotiations told The Associated Press on Sunday.

The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the agreement was subject to a successful physical.

Skubal’s deal, averaging $50 million annually, is the largest for a pitcher, topping Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million, 12-year contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers that started in 2024. The previous high for a pitcher’s average annual salary was $ 43.33 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.

It’s the fourth largest deal among all baseball players, trailing Juan Soto’s $765 million, Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million and Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s $500 million.

Skubal’s agreement includes a full no-trade clause and a $45 million signing bonus that is shielded from the management lockout that threatens the 2027 season, the person said.

He joins a Mets team that finished last in the NL East at 74-88 despite having baseball’s highest payroll on opening day at roughly $352 million. New York’s starters had a 4.47 ERA, ranking 23rd in the majors. Skubal will top a rotation featuring youngsters Nolan McLean and Christian Scott, with veterans Sean Manaea and Kodai Senga also under contract.

Skubal had plans to meet with at least six teams this month, including the Mets, Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres. His deal comes about a week before MLB owners are expected to lock out the players in a labor fight centering on management’s push for a salary cap. MLB has proposed a hard cap of $258.2 million for 2028. Skubal and Soto alone would account for nearly 40% of that cap.

A two-time All-Star left-hander who turned 30 on Nov. 20, Skubal is 43-17 with a 2.42 ERA in 88 starts over the last four seasons, striking out 655 and walking 95 in 546 innings.

New York high school students won't have to pass a Regents exam to graduate – but they will still be taking the Regents for the next three years.

State Education Department officials briefed the state Board of Regents recently on plans to meet federal Every Student Succeeds Act requirements. ESSA is the federal K-12 education law in the United States, signed in December 2015 to replace No Child Left Behind (NCLB).

The ESSA requires high school students to take one assessment in English language arts, math, science and social studies between ninth and 12th grades. The state Education Department plans to use the Regents tests to satisfy that requirement while a new set of high school assessment tests is developed. That should be done in time for tests in the spring of 2030.

"Maintaining these assessments during the transition provides the continuity for schools, districts, ensures that we’re able to have consistent and comparable information about our student achievement," said Zach Warner, assistant commissioner in the state Education Department's Office of State Assessment. "That continuity is especially important as we ask our districts to begin implementing other components of New York Inspires."

Much like testing in third through eighth grades, results of the Regents tests won't be part of a student's course grade. Instead, the tests will serve as a temperature check at the high school level, Warner said, to provide a common measure of student achievement across schools and school districts to allow the state to understand student outcomes around the state, identify disparities and determine where additional resources and support is needed. The purpose of statewide assessments under the ESSA is to make sure New York meets its federal obligations and doesn’t jeopardize federal funding the state receives while also providing a common statewide measure of student achievement, identify areas where there are issues and direct resources and support to fix those issues.

"So when we’re talking about the ESSA side of things, my piece here with the assessments, the requirement is for participation," Warner said. "There is not any required score that a student must achieve. Those may ask, 'Well, why should students participate in the exams if they’re not a requirement for the diploma?' And I need to point back to the work we’ve been doing, working with districts and talking about developing their local assessment strategies. Not every assessment that a teacher does goes directly into the grade book. So as we move towards a system that recognizes multiple ways for students to demonstrate their learning, we do have to preserve our ability to understand how our students are performing across the state to make those comparisons."

local.title: Silver Creek warns against on-street parking
local.summary: SILVER CREEK — With an eye on winter weather approaching soon, the Village of Silver Creek intends to crack down on violators of its local overnight parking law. The local law states that no vehicle shall be parked on any street or highway in the village between the hours of 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. […]
local.body:
SILVER CREEK -- With an eye on winter weather approaching soon, the Village of Silver Creek intends to crack down on violators of its local overnight parking law.

The local law states that no vehicle shall be parked on any street or highway in the village between the hours of 2 a.m. and 6 a.m. until April 1. The law is designed to keep the streets clear for plow trucks to clear the roadways, not only for efficiency, but also for the protection of vehicles and the safety of plow truck drivers. Many local municipalities have similar local laws, including the Village of Brocton, which employs the same Village Attorney as Silver Creek does, Peter Clark.

The Village intends to speak with the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office regarding enforcement of the law, and the Village Board is looking into issuing warnings for first-time offenders.

The Village is also evaluating the use of a night crew for the Department of Public Works again this year. The Board cited plowing of roads and sidewalks as reasoning for a night crew, especially to keep school-age children safe on the way to school. The Board will continue to discuss the matter in the coming weeks.

In another matter of parking in the village, a parking license agreement between the Village of Silver Creek and Plaza Group 304, LLC, was approved by the Village Board for use of the parking lot at 214 Central Ave., the site of the former Rite Aid building, from Nov. 16 through March 31, 2027. The Village agreed to handle plowing of the parking lot through the winter in exchange for the parking lot being available to the public.

Also at its latest meeting, the Village Board approved the purchase of a 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 Heavy Duty Work Truck, with a Fisher V-plow installed, for the Water/Sewer Department at a state bid cost of $63,481. The Village also declared two vehicles as surplus equipment to be sold at auction, a 2011 Ford F-350 pickup truck with a Western MVP Plow and a 1969 International Harvester paver. The truck has been replaced and the paver is not usable, according to Mayor Kathy Tampio.

The Board also authorized Tampio to sign an animal holding agreement with AnnMarie Hadley, of Forestville, pertaining to dog control services. A pair of budget modifications pertaining to insurance funds and village events were also recently approved.

The next meeting of the Silver Creek Village Board will be on Monday, Dec. 7 at 7 p.m. in the Village Boardroom.

local.title: SUNY Brockport employee is released from ICE custody on bond
local.summary: Germán Machado Guillen, a SUNY Brockport employee who was taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in mid-October, was released on bond on Nov. 20.
local.body:
Germán Machado Guillen, a SUNY Brockport employee who was taken into custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in mid-October, was released on bond Friday afternoon.

Machado Guillen's wife, Maria Velázquez, announced his release over the weekend, saying he had a bond hearing on Nov. 18 and was released two days later, after posting a $25,000 bond.

"We are celebrating Germán's return, but we also want to recognize every person who helped us get here," Velázquez said in a news release. "To those who took the time to care, to act, and to stand with an immigrant family during a frightening and uncertain time: thank you. Your actions made a difference in our lives. We hope our story reminds others that no family should have to face these circumstances alone."

Machado Guillen was taken into custody without warning by ICE agents outside his family home in Batavia in mid-October . Velázquez said that at the time Machado Guillen was arrested, he had a valid Employment Authorization Document to work at SUNY Brockport that expires in 2029. He is also listed on Velázquez’s pending asylum application, as are their two sons.

An ICE spokesperson previously told WXXI News that Machado Guillen's detention was part of a "targeted enforcement action." The agency alleged that the university staffer had overstayed his visa and remained living in the United States illegally, though with a valid work permit, for nearly a decade.

An EAD is issued by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services and allows a noncitizen to legally work in the U.S. for a specific period.

The document does not, by itself, establish a person’s immigration status or authorize them to remain in the country — a point ICE previously highlighted in its statement to WXXI News.

"To be clear,” the ICE statement read, “work authorization or a pending application does not confer legal status in the U.S.”

entertainment.title: Russell Brand’s Wife Vows to “Honor” Prison Rules After Relaying Message From Rapist Through YouTube
entertainment.summary: The video, in which Russell Brand proclaims his innocence, has not been taken down by YouTube despite requests from the U.K. government and widespread public outcry.
entertainment.body:
The wife of convicted rapist Russell Brand has vowed to “honor” prison rules after she came under fire for releasing a message for Brand via his YouTube channel.

While serving a 10-year and six-month sentence for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, the disgraced star told an online audience through his spouse: “I am not guilty [of] the offenses I have been jailed for.”

The video immediately drew criticism from the British public and U.K. government ministers who voiced concern for the welfare of Brand’s victims. “Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims,” said the country’s Justice Secretary Alex Norris at the time. “This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules.” Related Stories News Russell Brand Selling "Free Russell" Merch Via His Wellness Business While in Prison Movies Catholic Girls' School Thriller 'On Top of the Cliff' Wins Top Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival Award

Prime Minister Andy Burnham implored social media companies to “show some decency and take these videos down.” Officials sought to remove the video from Brand’s YouTube channel, with Google — the owner of the video platform — saying it was “aware of the new content and [that] our teams are investigating.” It added: “We suspended Russell Brand’s channel from the YouTube Partner Program in September 2023. The channel has not been able to monetise on YouTube since then.”

But the BBC reported last week that Google had declined a request from the Ministry of Justice to remove the video, saying none of its rules had been broken. At the time of publication, the video is still up on the site and has accrued over 1 million views.

Some outlets have speculated that Brand could face disciplinary action for the message, such as restrictions on phone calls, visitations, or other privilege losses.

On Sunday, Brand’s wife — who told the court during his six-week trial that he was a “caring and kind, wonderful father” — posted a new video to Sunday Service, saying: “Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention. […] Now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey [prison], I will absolutely honor that.”

However, The Hollywood Reporter reported over the weekend that the Brands are still selling merchandise calling for his freedom while he’s behind bars. The earliest reviews of the various products date to Nov. 16 (he was sentenced Nov. 9).

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Michael Douglas: 'I Have Loved And Lost. I Have Also Loved And Won With...'
entertainment.summary: A Hollywood legend, Michael Douglas has lived virtually his entire romantic career in the public eye, which gives him a unique perspective on relationships.
entertainment.body:
While he landed a few film and TV roles in the '60s and early '70s, it was crime drama "The Streets of San Francisco" that served as Douglas' big break. But if the 1972 cop series (that still holds up today) put Douglas on the map, it was his Oscar-winning production work on 1975's "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" that launched his career into the stratosphere.

Douglas went on to amass a staggering number of credits, both in front of and behind the camera. He received another Academy Award, this time for best actor in 1987's "Wall Street." He also won an Emmy in 2013 for "Behind the Candelabra," alongside several nominations over the years for shows like "Will & Grace" and "The Kominsky Method." While they didn't earn him statuettes, Douglas is also known for projects like "Fatal Attraction," "Romancing the Stone," and his recent turn as Benjamin Franklin in Apple TV's "Franklin."

Last month, Douglas released a memoir titled "One Helluva Ride," documenting his illustrious career, as well as his relationships with his father, his son, and his wife of over two decades, Catherine Zeta-Jones. Douglas is a true Hollywood legend. That's why he's today's quote of the day.

Static Media "I have loved and lost. I have also loved and won with my partner for life, Catherine."

The above quote comes from the conclusion of Michael Douglas' memoir. In a conversation about the new book with Good Morning America , the actor discussed his 26-year relationship with fellow Academy Award winner and "Wednesday" star Catherine Zeta-Jones, including a period where the two were separated. "We both had to change," Douglas said. "And sometimes I think it's just good to kind of call time out and just talk as two human beings."

The timeout worked. Now, Douglas is even more confident in his relationship with Zeta-Jones. "I love Catherine in a way that I have never loved any other woman," Douglas wrote in "One Helluva Ride" (via Entertainment Weekly ). "She's my wife, my best friend, and my life partner. I could never lose her."

lev radin/Shutterstock We all go through rough patches in life. Between his high-profile divorce from first wife Diandra Luker, stage IV cancer diagnosis in 2010, and experience with both his son's addiction and his own, Michael Douglas has lived through more hard times than many. Despite all this pain, however, Douglas' marriage proved to be resilient. Sometimes it may seem like there's no end to the darkness, but with time — and maybe even a brief timeout — true love can overcome even the direst obstacles.

Warner Bros. Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The most magical part about the "Harry Potter" story is the friendship between Harry, Hermione Granger, and Ron Weasley, but the Hogwarts staff are also major pillars within the narrative. We've already had character posters for the main trio, and now HBO has unveiled a batch of posters highlighting four important figures at the famous school of witchcraft and wizardry.

Rubeus Hagrid (Nick Frost), a Hogwarts gamekeeper who had his wand broken after being expelled from Hogwarts for an offence he didn't commit many years earlier, holds the umbrella that disguises its remnants.

The "Harry Potter" TV series, which will be "a faithful adaptation" of the beloved seven-book series penned by J.K. Rowling, according to a press release, is set to release on HBO and HBO Max on Christmas Day, 2026. The first season follows the plot of Rowling's first Potter book, "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone."

View this post on Instagram While HBO's "Harry Potter" series has inspired a wave of excitement from OG Potter readers and newcomers alike, it's also attracted quite a bit of negativity from some factions of fans. From the backlash over Paapa Essiedu's casting as Snape to complaints about the scope of J.K. Rowling's involvement due to her political opinions , it seems each week brings new things for fans to debate. Now, the new Hogwarts staff character posters featuring Dumbledore, McGonagall, Snape and Hagrid are also drawing complaints from fans.

One of the main grievances is the look of Dumbledore's Elder wand, which is very basic in its design. In the films, the Elder wand, which is the most powerful wand of its kind, looks much more intricate. Although HBO's design is actually closer to what Rowling described in the book series, it seems that fans aren't exactly impressed. "The ELDER WAND is just a stick!?" one commenter wrote . "Elder wand? This series is an absolute joke I swear," wrote a second. Meanwhile, a third took issue with all of the wands. "Noooooo. Their wands are horrible. Despite the mixed receptions to the promotional materials, the "Harry Potter" series has already been renewed by HBO for a second season .

entertainment.body:
Ian “Molly” Meldrum will be honored with a state funeral, as tributes pour in from across the music world for the Australian broadcaster and record producer, who died Monday (Nov. 23) in Melbourne at 83. Explore Jimmy Barnes Kylie Minogue Tina Arena See latest videos, charts and news

Kylie Minogue , who appeared on Meldrum’s Countdown as a teenager at the start of her career, remembered him as one of her earliest inspirations. Related Molly Meldrum, Australian Music Broadcaster and 'Countdown' Host, Dies at 83 Fans Choose LISA's 'Leave With Me' as This Week's Favorite New Music ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6'

“He championed so many Aussie artists and welcomed international artists to Australia in his own wonderful and inimitable way,” she wrote. “I’m so grateful for his unwavering love and support. Vale Molly. I’m going to turn the music up in your honour.”

Jimmy Barnes offered the most complicated tribute, recalling that Meldrum was initially an adversary — “running the best music TV show in the country but insisting that we had to mime.” The relationship changed. “Molly exposed us to a huge music audience we could never have reached, and we were always thankful to him for that,” Barnes wrote on Instagram.

Tina Arena , a longtime friend, posted a gallery of images. “I’m deeply saddened by the passing of Molly Meldrum , a man who made an incredible contribution to the music industry in Australia and abroad,” she wrote. “My deepest condolences go out to his family and friends.”

Iva Davies of Icehouse wrote on X that Meldrum “was such a bright, larger-than-life figure in our Australian music scene for so many years with positive influence on so many careers via his work on Countdown , as a journalist, producer, advocate and friend.” He added: “Like the rest of the music community that owed so much to his support, the band and I are so thankful that Molly was a part of our lives and music.”

Darren Hayes of Savage Garden wrote that he doesn’t “remember a day in my life without Molly Meldrum being a part of it.”

Jason Donovan called him “a truly unique character, a great Australian and one of this country’s greatest pioneers and ambassadors for music and entertainment.” He added: “He was loved, recognised and respected around the world for the extraordinary contribution he made to Australian music and the artists he championed. There will never be another quite like him.”

entertainment.title: Inside Stockholm’s Gasometer, Europe’s Most Ambitious New Music Venue: ‘This Will Create Waves Far Beyond Here’
entertainment.summary: The venue will host its opening performances in March 2027.
entertainment.body:
On a frigid November morning, Julien Planté , head of music at Miramis, and the team lead a preview tour of Gasometer, a new venue in Stockholm that’s slated to open in March 2027. Sections of the site are finished, while in others, we sidle between boxes and pallets of wood, and peer over red tape while the site undergoes its legal assessments.

Inside the venue, the scale of the venture becomes clear; our guide says that she’s starstruck every day when she comes into the space. We enter by the rear stage door, facing the pristine, pillarless seated auditorium. It’s easy to see why she feels that way. Related Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support -- For Now -- to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight Bill Donahue

“Gasometer is not just for Stockholm, or Sweden or the Nordic countries, but for the whole of Europe,” says Planté.

The space features two venues: a main auditorium and a second, more intimate venue built into the Gasometer’s roof meant primarily for intimate gatherings,banquets and dinners. Miramis estimates that the investment into the project so far has totaled €100 million ($109 million).

The venue’s first main space, called Theatre, features three levels of stalls seating and a standing area which is customizable depending on the production. In a theatre format, the room accommodates 1,750 guests and up to 2,300 with floor standing.

Planté speaks proudly of the significance of this venture, which was undertaken by Miramis, the entertainment and hospitality group that already operates the city’s popular Cirkus venue in the Djurgårdsslätten district. Miramis is a sister company to Pophouse Entertainment, a private entertainment company, co-founded by ABBA ’s Björn Ulvaeus, which launched the wildly successful ABBA Voyage show in London.

Gasometer will arrive at a time when some of the world’s leading acts are emerging from a variety of countries in Europe, such as RAYE (U.K.), Rosalía (Spain) and Zara Larsson (Sweden). The venue aims to be a standard bearer for creative innovation in the European venue scene, combining the programming diversity of London’s Southbank Centre with the technological advances of Manchester’s Co-op Live and Aviva Studios.

The venue is an ambitious and dazzling undertaking. It repurposes one of two former gasworks in the city’s northern district, and is part of a wider development of the area bringing living and work spaces to Stockholm in an area that was first built in 1899 to supply the city’s growing need for energy, and was eventually decommissioned a century later in 2011.

entertainment.body:
You Can See Everything continues visualizing box office success at a level that puts it in elite company as a documentary .

Focusing on disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes ‘ life in the lead-up to her prison sentence, A24 ‘s film surpassed $100 million globally over the weekend, a rare feat for any documentary. After opening Oct. 16 in North America, directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ‘s three-hour feature has grossed $93.4 million domestically over its six weekends in release and has more recently been rolling out in international markets. It becomes the 19th movie released in 2026 to join the “One Million Watched Club,” and with its 4.61 average Letterboxd rating, it is the second-highest-rated feature to hit the milestone, behind only 12 Angry Men with 4.63. You Can See Everything is the highest-rated 2026 film and the second-highest-rated documentary ever, trailing only Stop Making Sense on the social platform.

Among the box office achievements for You Can See Everything include opening with $15.6 million in its debut frame to register the second-biggest domestic launch for a non-music documentary, behind 2004’s Fahrenheit 9/11 . The Holmes documentary also scored the highest-grossing domestic opening weekend for a release in fewer than 1,000 theaters since 2006’s Borat . The movie remains the second-highest-grossing domestic non-music documentary, with only Fahrenheit 9/11 and its $119.1 million cume to beat.

entertainment.title: The Gilded Age's Louisa Jacobson Reacts To Marian's Season 4 Discovery: 'I Loved The Way That She Finds Out'
entertainment.summary: Marian comes to a shocking conclusion on Sunday's episode of The Gilded Age, and Louisa Jacobson tells TVLine what she "loved" about the a-ha moment.
entertainment.body:
Warning: This interview spoils the events of "The Gilded Age" Season 4, Episode 4. Proceed at your own risk.

Random bleeding is never a good sign for a TV character, especially on a period drama like "The Gilded Age," where a mere a drop of blood on a napkin could signal someone's imminent demise. But as Marian discovers on Sunday's episode, it could also be a symptom of something else entirely.

After initially dismissing her nosebleeds, insisting she's just been overworking herself, Marian has a frank talk with Nurse Virginia (Elizabeth Marvel). Marian's new friend asks if she's due for her "monthly courses," an old-timey way of referring to menstruation, as some women do experience nosebleeds around that time. This stops Marian dead in her tracks, as she quickly comes to the realization that she hasn't had her "monthly," in addition to feeling strange as of late.

"That can't be, can it?" Marian asks, alluding to a possible pregnancy, and Virginia replies with the obvious follow-up question: "Is there any reason to believe that it could?" Um, there sure is! Marian and Larry infamously shared a night together in the "Gilded Age" Season 4 premiere , and she's been carrying the shame of their premarital romp ever since. And now it seems she's carrying quite a bit more!

"I loved the way that she finds out," actress Louisa Jacobson tells TVLine. "The writers wanted to make sure it wasn't an obvious thing with the nosebleeds. They could have done puking and stuff, but they chose nosebleeds, which isn't totally a widely known symptom of pregnancy."

As for Marian's "a-ha!" moment, Jacobson says that scene between her and Marvel was one of her favorite scenes to film, because "you really see the lack of education that women had around this kind of thing, and how lost Marian really is as an orphan, as someone who didn't have any examples of healthy family dynamics, or even an understanding of how babies are made. You see in that moment how childlike she is, and how alone she is."

HBO As Louisa Jacobson points out, "The Gilded Age" could have had given Marian morning sickness to foreshadow her pregnancy, but the writers opted to give her a nosebleed instead. As it turns out, the reason behind that particular symptom is two-fold.

On a more obvious level, executive producer Sonja Warfield tells TVLine that she gave Marian nosebleeds because she "wanted viewers to think something else" was wrong with her, adding, "I did not want them to immediately think she was pregnant."

Missoni pillows, a dark chocolate square and a pour of Blanton’s single-barrel bourbon isn’t just reserved for hotel turn-down service anymore — it’s also the new standard for Delta travelers flying in the airline’s Delta One cabin.

The U.S. airline unveiled its so-called “next era” of Delta One last month, with food and hospitality offerings that aim to position Delta as the “industry’s most premium end-to-end travel experience,” according to a release.

The new offerings include a reimagined Delta One menu, with a wagyu brioche burger among the highlights, along with a Hong Kong-style sea bass, Japanese grilled salmon and a “seasonally rotating” risotto dish, all served on new Delta-branded tableware. Lopez made the remarks in an interview with The New York Times , pushing back on the notion that she gets thousands of acting offers, claiming instead that Hollywood has often overlooked her because of her ethnicity.

“Even from the beginning of my career, I got offered things, but I was only offered a few things. I had to kind of create things for myself,” the actress said. “And the reason, I think, is because I just wasn’t the typical kind of, like, to be honest, a white actress. You know what I mean? And it’s still kind of the same today.”

Lopez’s more recent film credits include “Office Romance” (2026), “Shotgun Wedding” (2022), “Hustlers” (2019) and “Second Act” (2018).

She also secured several leading roles in the late 1990s and early 2000s, including “The Wedding Planner,” “Out of Sight” and “Maid in Manhattan,” and was cast as the late singer Selena Quintanilla-Perez in “Selena.”

The Puerto Rican actress said Hollywood continues to look for “certain” things when casting performers, suggesting that the industry’s preferences have historically made it more difficult for actors of color to secure roles.

Lopez acknowledged, however, that the screen industry has made progress in improving diversity and representation.

“There’s a certain thing that they look for, and it’s more diverse now for sure, and that’s good,” the actress said.

entertainment.summary: Some half-hour comedy shows don't hold up a decade or two removed from their respective heydays - others stand the test of time remarkably well.
entertainment.body:
