Well before we had modern classics like "The Office," there were several series on the air that managed to delight audiences and continue to do so.

Here is our ranking of some of the best classic sitcoms from the '70s and '80s that get better every time you watch them, all while providing a healthy dose of nostalgia. These five sitcoms were ahead of their time in their portrayals of complex yet entertaining characters navigating everything from retirement to neighbors with poor boundaries. Some of these are remembered as some of the best shows of all time .

NBC No one can forget the iconic "Golden Girls" theme song: "Thank You for Being a Friend." The classic NBC sitcom premiered over 40 years ago, and the way it highlights the best and worst parts of true friendship still holds up to the test of time.

Starring Bea Arthur, Betty White, Rue McClanahan and Estelle Getty, "The Golden Girls" follows a group of women living together in Miami as they navigate the woes of romance, aging, and womanhood together. Each of the lead actresses won an Emmy Award for their performance on the long-running show, and it's easy to see why. The series was unafraid to tackle politics and social topics in between laughs, making for a refreshing rewatch. Between White's dazed and confused Rose, Arthur's ever-practical Dorothy and her strong-willed mother Sophia (Getty), and McClanahan's romantic and vivacious Blanche, "The Golden Girls" delivers surprisingly fast-paced humor for sleepy Florida.

NBC "Cheers" carefully walks the line between workplace comedy and hangout sitcom thanks to its iconic location at the eponymous Boston bar owned by Ted Danson's character Sam Malone. By far, what helps "Cheers" work is that the bar regulars come with their own complicated baggage, allowing their storylines to tie together meaningfully with the show's signature banter. From Dr. Frasier Crane (Kelsey Grammer) helping Sam overcome his addiction to Sam's on-and-off relationship with Diane (Shelley Long), "Cheers" feels especially relatable and human. The sitcom's sharp sense of humor never fails, even when touching upon relevant topics such as class and feminism.

The NBC series, which ran for 11 seasons, helped launch the careers for many actors we know and love, from Danson to Rhea Perlman, Kirstie Alley and Woody Harrelson.

entertainment.title: 15 Best Sci-Fi Shows Of The '80s, Ranked
entertainment.summary: The '80s were a great time for sci-fi, so it's no surprise that the decade produced some standout TV series that are still worth checking out today.
entertainment.body:
NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The '80s are typically thought of as a fantastic decade for sci-fi. The original "Star Wars" and "Star Trek" movies were still debuting on the big screen, alongside awesome new properties like "Tron," "The Last Starfighter" and "Enemy Mine." The president of the United States was so fascinated by the possibilities that he imagined an outer space-based missile shield could save the world. And on TV... well, the special effects budgets weren't quite so big, but the high concepts flew fast and furiously.

In considering the best sci-fi TV shows of this decade, we find both genuinely great, thoughtful science fiction and amazingly entertaining cheese. Sometimes, comedy in them is intentional and brilliant; other times, it may be accidental, but at least it's committed. This list does stick to live-action only — animated sci-fi shows in the '80s weren't quite ready for primetime, and we have a whole separate rundown of the 15 best sci-fi cartoons of all time .

From the goofy to the glorious, and the educated to the excessive. here are the best sci-fi shows of the '80s, ranked.

Metromedia Video Productions If someone impersonated a stereotypical robot voice in the '80s, chances are they were impersonating V.I.C.I., the robot girl at the center of the sitcom "Small Wonder." In the tradition of other magically powered family member sitcoms from "Bewitched" to "My Favorite Martian," "Small Wonder" has its unique character be a kid for once. The premise is that the robot is supposed to help disabled children, so its inventor integrated it with his own family to allow it to learn while masquerading as a new adopted daughter.

Unlike the abrasive A.L.F. in a similar sitcom — which is definitely not on this list — Tiffany Brissette is charming as the robot who wants to learn to be human. Over the course of the show, she even gets a genuine arc, as the onscreen robot character has to adapt to Brissette's actual growth spurts. As with many alien and android characters of the era, it's also now possible to read her character as representing viewers on the spectrum. Brissette would later leave acting to become a nurse .

ABC Relative to the movie it's loosely based on, "Blue Thunder" could be seen as a travesty. The film, which is still timely, is about how police shouldn't have access to military-grade vehicles. The TV show, on the other hand, is about how awesome things might be if they did. You have super-helicopter Blue Thunder, piloted by Frank Chaney (James Farentino) and Clinton C. Wonderlove (a pre-comedy Dana Carvey) in the sky; and Rolling Thunder, a van with a dune buggy inside, driven by two guys named Bubba and Ski, played by former football stars Bubba Smith and Dick Butkus. "Knight Rider" may have had a similar truck, and "Airwolf" a similar chopper, but "Blue Thunder" had both, plus two football players trying to act and a future comedy icon trying to be serious. It was awesomely entertaining in a very '80s way.

entertainment.summary: The gentleman widely known as Captain Kirk dabbled in New Zealand children's television during the late '90s, and the results won't cost you a dime.

As The Storyteller in New Zealand's "A Twist in the Tale," Shatner introduced kids to wild stories of time travel, mysterious diaries, and buried treasure. Each of the 15 episodes had tales for kids akin to fellow horror anthology TV shows "The Twilight Zone" and "Are You Afraid of the Dark?" Best of all, it's streaming free on Tubi and Pluto TV.

The single season of "A Twist in the Tale" launched several careers. Chelsie Preston Crayford recently played the lead in the mystery whodunnit series "A Remarkable Place to Die" and Peter Hambleton played Gloin in all three "Hobbit" films.

A Twist in the Tale/Cloud 9 Don't let the name of his role in "The Twist in the Tale" fool you. As The Storyteller, William Shatner isn't just speaking to the camera to lightly introduce the plot like Rod Serling in "The Twilight Zone." At the beginning of each episode, he talks with a group of children, telling them interesting facts and asking them questions as if he was an elementary school teacher.

In the first episode, "Obsession in August," he takes a group through a home library filled with books and artifacts. Brandishing a sword, he tells the children about King Arthur and the knights of the round table. Earlier this year, Bullock opened up about how her children navigated Randall’s health battle and recalled how Louis and Laila “could see” what was happening. “They’re very, very astute kids,” she said during an August appearance on the “Smartless” podcast. “They not only see the physical change, there’s a behavior that changes in all of us. However, there are sometimes supporting characters that just win the hearts and minds of the audience and become more of a focus as the series goes on. In certain cases, these characters can be so interesting that they usurp control of the story away from the original lead.

Sitcoms where supporting characters become main characters are one thing, but a change like this in a drama can have much bigger ramifications due to the genre's more serious nature and higher narrative stakes. This kind of unexpected evolution of a side character's importance can completely change a show's trajectory. Here are five drama series with side characters who went on to become central characters.

Netflix "Stranger Things" is filled to the brim with homages to '80s pop culture and Steve Harrington (Joe Keery) fills in the classic jock-bully archetype perfectly. In the first season, he serves as a recurring antagonist to Charlie Heaton's Jonathan Byers. Narratively, Steve functions as a human obstacle for Jonathan to overcome when not dealing with supernatural stuff. While Steve shows some admirable qualities and stands up to the Demogorgon at the end of Season 1, he is a supporting character outside of the central ensemble. The aspects of the character that shine through his bully role endeared him to audiences, making it all the more natural for him to become a central character in subsequent seasons.

After leaving behind his bully persona, Steve shows great emotional growth and becomes a role model that many of the characters look up to, especially Gaten Matarazzo's Dustin Henderson. The brotherly bond between these two is a central part of the show's narrative in later seasons. It also functions as a way for Steve to show how much Steve has broken away from the letterman jacket-wearing stereotype.

Grogu, aka "Baby Yoda," was present from the very first episode of "The Mandalorian" on Disney+ and audiences became enamored with the infant. The fanfare from the fanbase for the debut of a new strange alien in "Star Wars" canon was as expected, but the level of fame Grogu went on to garner was much more than anyone could have imagined.

entertainment.title: Molly Meldrum, Australian Music Broadcaster and ‘Countdown’ Host, Dies at 83
entertainment.summary: "Affectionately dubbed 'The Guru,' Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," his family said in a statement.
entertainment.body:
Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian broadcaster, journalist and record producer whose weekly television show made stars of international and local acts alike, died Monday (Nov. 23) at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne. He was 83. Explore ABBA Elton John Kylie Minogue See latest videos, charts and news

His family said he died peacefully after a long period of ill health. “Affectionately dubbed ‘The Guru,’ Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music,” they said in a statement. “He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them.” He is survived by his long-term partner, Yan Wongngam. Related Fans Choose LISA's 'Leave With Me' as This Week's Favorite New Music ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With 'GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6' Selena Gomez Helps Couple With Baby's Sex Reveal at Spurs Game, 'With No Hesitation'

From 1974 to 1987, Meldrum presented Countdown , the ABC’s Sunday-evening music program, which he co-created with executive producer Michael Shrimpton and producer-director Robbie Weekes. Across 563 episodes, it became appointment viewing for young Australians, and — years before MTV — a showcase that leaned heavily on music video.

The Australian Recording Industry Association said Monday that Meldrum had spent six decades convincing a country raised on British and American records that its own artists could stand alongside the greats.

That reach extended well beyond Australia . ABBA broke there on the strength of clips Meldrum played after their 1974 Eurovision win, scoring six No. 1 singles within two years, with “Fernando” spending 14 weeks atop the chart. “Molly started playing our videos down in Australia and it seemed as though the rest of the world just woke up,” Björn Ulvaeus later said. Madonna landed her first hit single anywhere in April 1984, when “Holiday” aired on the show. Blondie , Cyndi Lauper , Meat Loaf , John Mellencamp and Boz Scaggs all found early Australian audiences the same way.

At home, his endorsement moved records. When Meldrum told viewers to “do yourself a favour” on a Sunday night, ARIA said record stores braced for a hectic Monday. Countdown turned Skyhooks and Sherbet into national names and gave early platforms to AC/DC , INXS , Olivia Newton-John , Divinyls, Icehouse and a teenage Kylie Minogue . Elton John , a longtime friend, has called Meldrum the best thing that ever happened to Australian music.

HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It's deceptively easy to distinguish what exactly a villain on "The Sopranos" is. After all, the show's protagonist is a narcissistic mob boss who lies, steals, and murders with little to no meaningful remorse. David Chase did give Tony (James Gandolfini) fair competition in terms of pure evil: an old-school psychopath challenging him for power; a sadistic capo who seemingly existed just to cause torment in other people's lives; even Tony's own twisted mother.

At the same time, some of the "villains" in Tony's life are far more sympathetic than he is. From the boss who challenged New Jersey's obvious dysfunction to the friend he failed to save, there are arcs where it's hard not to root for these characters to pull through. What unites every kind of villain on "The Sopranos" are their satisfying character arcs, rich psychological backgrounds, and indelible impact on the show's biggest events.

"The Sopranos" is a show about a monster, so it's easy to forget how many other monsters David Chase sent after him. Over six seasons, Tony Soprano survived rival bosses, double-crossing soldiers, and reckless upstarts, but the show's most dangerous enemies were rarely the ones with the highest body counts. More often, they were the ones sitting at his dinner table. We've ranked the best villains in the series (not including guest stars) with these qualities in mind. This is your first and only warning for major spoilers for all six seasons of "The Sopranos."

HBO Jackie Jr. (Jason Cerbone) is a flash-in-the-pan villain — a troubled supporting character who could've become Tony Soprano's next protege, and instead wound up being one of his most tragic victims. The son of the late boss (Michael Rispoli's Jackie Aprile) is introduced toward the end of Season 2 as a steady example of what a child raised by a mobster — but decidedly outside the mob lifestyle — could become. The sad beauty of his character arc is that Jackie Jr. proves how superficial the line between those two actually is.

Though Tony honors his friend's wish that he not be allowed into the family, Jackie is still his father's son. He's reckless, arrogant, and coldly womanizing (despite initial chivalry and charm, he treats Meadow Soprano terribly and is ultimately caught cheating on her). This was all before he grabbed himself a gun and made the decision to try and shoot his way into the game. It shows how Jackie's father, his pseudo-stepfather, Ralph (Joe Pantoliano), and Tony rubbed off on him — they all thought that they could behave however they wanted without that behavior impacting their children. Jackie's arc foreshadows the dysfunctional life AJ Soprano (Robert Iler) grows into in the following seasons.

entertainment.title: Harrison Ford's First TV Credit Was In This Classic '60s Western Series
entertainment.summary: As implausible as it sounds now, at one point, Harrison Ford played second banana to John Saxon when they were both struggling young actors.
entertainment.body:
Determined to pursue his acting dreams, Ford booked a minor role in a Season 5 episode of the NBC series entitled "The Modoc Kid." The actor played Cullen Tindall, an outlaw who helps hold the Grainger family hostage after his crew — led by a ne'er-do-well played by John Saxon — attempts to rob a bank. The guest-starring role included several lines of dialogue and a shootout with one of the show's main characters, Stacey Grainger (Don Quine).

The actor found himself back on the frontier in 2022 when he played Dutton family patriarch Jacob Dutton on Taylor Sheridan's Paramount+ series "1923." The Western drama, set in the "Yellowstone" universe, follows Ford's Jacob as he fights for his livelihood during Prohibition and the Great Depression alongside his wife, Cara (Helen Mirren). Ford told The Hollywood Reporter in 2025 that he loves several aspects of the Western genre.

"I love the viscerality of it, I love the physical nature of the storytelling, I love being in natural circumstances," Ford explained, adding that Westerns have "a kind of old-fashioned movie-making... — mostly, no CGI or very little CGI — a little something to sweeten the location. But it's really essential, old-time storytelling and I love working with this kind of material."

entertainment.title: Fans Choose LISA’s ‘Leave With Me’ as This Week’s Favorite New Music
entertainment.summary: Her latest solo release brought in more than 84% of the vote.
entertainment.body:
“Leave With Me,” the emotional new solo single released by LISA of BLACKPINK , tops this week’s new music poll.

Listeners voted in a poll published Friday (Nov. 20) on Billboard , choosing LISA’s latest track as their favorite new music.

“Leave With Me” topped new releases from TOMORROW X TOGETHER, Gracie Abrams and more on the poll, and it rose above the Grand Theft Auto VI album, which features songs by a number of stars: Cardi B, Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Playboi Carti, Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala and many others — including BLACKPINK member JENNIE (with “Power Trip”). At the poll’s closing time on Sunday, LISA’s new ballad had a landslide victory, bringing in more than 84% of the vote.

“Leave With Me” plays over the end credits of LISA’s Always Lalisa documentary about the rise of her career of a solo artist outside of girl group BLACKPINK. The doc, directed by Sue Kim, is now available to stream exclusively on YouTube Premium.

The song, officially released this week, was co-written by LISA, Feli Ferraro, Tyler Spry, Ali Tamposi and Shintaro Yasuda.

“The only way forward is through,” she sings, leading up to the chorus: “I’ma take yesterday, kiss it goodbye/ Wipe my eyes dry, hold my head high/ I leave with me/ Check the clock, yeah, it’s my time/ Spread my wings, fly, me on my side/ You know that there’s no hard feelings/ Every wrong and right, put me right where I’m supposed to be/ No hard feelings/ And you can come or stay, either way, I’ma leave with me.”

Prior to its release, LISA had surprised fans with the live debut of the then-unknown “Leave With Me” during opening night of her six-show “Viva La Lisa” residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.

Trailing behind “Leave With Me” on the poll are TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s “Angel Bite,” with 8% of the vote, and the multi-artist Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album , with 2% of the vote.

sports.title: Jahmyr Gibbs has 52 career rushing TDs, ties Barry Sanders for most before turning 25
sports.summary: Two Lions running backs now share the NFL record for the most rushing touchdowns before turning 25 years old.
sports.body:
Jahmyr Gibbs scored his 51st and 52nd career rushing touchdowns on Sunday against the Buccaneers, which ties him with Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns by a player under the age of 25 in NFL history.

Gibbs doesn’t turn 25 until after this season, so if he scores just one more rushing touchdown this year, he’ll move ahead of Sanders and have the record to himself. It’s safe to say Gibbs will score at least one more in the Lions’ seven remaining games. Sunday was Gibbs’ 18th game with multiple touchdowns, and he now has 62 total touchdowns in 59 career games.

Gibbs is the betting favorite to win the NFL’s Offensive Player of the Year award. He has 1,502 scrimmage yards and 15 touchdowns this season, both leading the league.

sports.title: 49ers lose right tackle Colton McKivitz for season with fractured, dislocated ankle
sports.summary: The 49ers lost starting right tackle Colton McKivitz for the season on Sunday night with a serious ankle injury.
sports.body:
Coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed the injury after the game and said it was particularly hard for the 49ers to see McKivitz get hurt because of how well respected he is within the locker room.

“That was really crushing. Colton’s had an unbelievable year. We care about all our guys, but it was tough to see Colton go down like that,” Shanahan said.

Shanahan said McKivitz appears to have the same injury that 49ers linebacker Fred Warner suffered last year. Warner had that injury in Week 6 and missed the rest of the season, so McKivitz will certainly not be able to play again this season after suffering the injury in Week 11.

“We think it’s broken and dislocated, similar to Fred’s last year,” Shanahan said.

McKivitz suffered the injury midway through the second quarter and was replaced by Vederian Lowe. Shanahan said Lowe played well for the rest of the game and the 49ers will be counting on him to play well for the rest of the season.

sports.title: Sunday Night Football: 49ers move to 9-1 with dominant 35-10 victory over Vikings
sports.summary: George Kittle caught two touchdowns as San Francisco became the first team to score at least 30 points against Minnesota in 2026.
sports.body:
Sunday night’s victory over the Vikings makes for a great argument that they are.

San Francisco put together a dominant performance against Minnesota, coming away with a 35-10 victory in Mexico City.

The 49ers were impressive on both offense and defense, but the result from the former was particularly notable. It’s the first time Minnesota has allowed 30 points all year, with only two teams reaching 20 points prior to Sunday’s contest.

Quarterback Brock Purdy had an excellent night, finishing 21-of-26 for 255 yards with three touchdowns. Head coach Kyle Shanahan took him out of the game midway through the fourth quarter with the contest effectively decided.

George Kittle caught the first two touchdowns of the night, with Mike Evans catching Purdy’s third late in the second quarter. The 49ers then scored again on Ji’Ayir Brown’s pick-six off Kirk Cousins to hold a 28-10 lead at halftime.

Running back Christian McCaffrey added a 6-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter to cap a 13-play, 98-yard drive that put the game out of reach.

McCaffrey finished with 49 yards on 12 carries with a TD. He also caught two passes for 13 yards.

Evans had six catches for 109 yards with a score, Keenan Allen caught three passes for 38 yards, and Kittle finished with three receptions for 34 yards with two TDs.

sports.title: Christian McCaffrey touchdown gives 49ers 35-10 lead in fourth quarter
sports.summary: It's just about all but over in Mexico City. 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey capped a 13-play, 98-yard drive with a 6-yard touchdown to give San Francisco a 35-10 lead with 13:26 left in the fourth quarter.
sports.body:
49ers running back Christian McCaffrey capped a 13-play, 98-yard drive with a 6-yard touchdown to give San Francisco a 35-10 lead with 13:26 left in the fourth quarter.

Minnesota had put San Francisco on the 2-yard line with a well-covered punt. But San Francisco was nevertheless able to methodically make its way down the field, converting three third downs on the way to the end zone.

Newly acquired Keenan Allen caught two of the third-down conversions, moving the chains on third-and-4 with an 8-yard catch and on third-and-9 with a 13-yard reception.

The drive covered 7:04 across the third and fourth quarters, putting Minnesota in an even more unfavorable position as the team tries to get back in it.

McCaffrey now has 11 rushing touchdowns this season along with three receiving TDs.

sports.title: Jevón Holland on controversial Parker Washington call: "Shoutout Vegas"
sports.summary: Back when the NFL hated gambling, it feared that widespread legalized sports betting would prompt fans to think the fix is in.
sports.body:
Giants safety Jevón Holland went there on Sunday, regarding the decision that Jaguars receiver Parker Washington failed to catch what would have been a touchdown pass in the fourth quarter.

“The game’s over? That might have been a catch,” Holland said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post. “That was a hell of a play. When they called it out, I was like, ‘Alright.’ Shoutout Vegas , man. I don’t know.”

Holland was surely joke. On the topic of suggesting that something fishy was happening, however, the NFL may not have a sense of humor.

It’s precisely the kind of comment to which the tinfoil-hat crowd will cling. Even if Holland doesn’t mean it, those who want to think the fix is in will seize on the statement of evidence that the fix is in.

As we’ve said time and again, the fix isn’t in. However, the NFL needs to be far more concerned about that perception than it is.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers calls DK Metcalf's ejection "disappointing," won't comment on message to him
sports.summary: On certain subjects, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers doesn't stop talking.
sports.body:
Regarding Sunday’s ejection of Steelers receiver DK Metcalf from the 19-16 loss to the Eagles, Rodgers said far close to nothing than something.

“ That was disappointing ,” Rodgers told reporters. “Obviously, we love DK. And I don’t know what was going on out there, what was happening. But, yeah, we can’t have two of those.”

“I’m not going to tell you that,” Rodgers said. “I’m going to talk to DK. We’re real good friends, so.”

The “I’m not going to tell you that” was unnecessary, but on brand. Rodgers flashes that aspect of his personality from time to time. And it surely will make those who have to ask him questions on a regular basis not miss him after he retires following the current season.

Besides, why is it such a secret? Rodgers already said it was “disappointing” and that “we can’t have” that. He could have just said that’s the message.

Really, what else would the message be? Metcalf needs to control his emotions. Given that Rodgers has been willing to call out others when it’s required, why should Metcalf be exempt?

Maybe that’s exactly what Metcalf needs in order to keep him from doing it again.

sports.title: Sunday Night Football: 49ers lead Vikings 28-10 at halftime
sports.summary: QB Brock Purdy threw three TD passes in the first half, two of which went to TE George Kittle.
sports.body:
Through two quarters, they sure look like the conference’s best team.

San Francisco leads Minnesota 28-10 at halftime in Mexico City.

The 49ers scored touchdowns on three of their first four possessions, getting two TD catches from George Kittle before Mike Evans found the end zone for a 4-yard score in his first game since Oct. 19.

But the 49ers got another score within 10 seconds of game time, as after Evans’ score, safety Ji’Ayir Brown picked off Kirk Cousins and returned it 18 yards to the end zone for a pick-six.

It was Cousins’ fourth interception thrown to the 49ers in two games this season, though the first matchup came when the quarterback was with the Raiders.

Cousins finished the first half 12-of-19 passing for 121 yards with the pick. T.J. Hockenson leads with 40 yards on four catches while Justin Jefferson has 36 yards on two receptions.

The Vikings had two more chances to put up points, as Will Reichard missed a pair of field goals. The first was more realistic than the second, as he sent a 55-yard attempt wide left. But Reichard also had a 71-yard attempt to end the half with a fair catch/free kick situation. Reichard’s last attempt fell just short.

49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan has gotten the better of Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores to this point in the game. The numbers are solid across the board for San Francisco, but emblematic of the team’s success is that the offense faced just three third downs in the first half. The 49ers were 1-of-3 in the category.

Players from both San Francisco and Minnesota were visibly upset on the field by the sight of the injury.

sports.title: NFL says Parker Washington didn't control ball until he was out of bounds
sports.summary: Sunday's game between the Jaguars and Giants included a controversial decision in the fourth quarter on a play that looked like a touchdown catch by Jacksonville receiver Parker Washington.
sports.body:
The ruling on the field was that the catch was incomplete. Jaguars coach Liam Coen challenged the decision.

Replay review confirmed the ruling on the field, even though CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore said during the broadcast that he believed it was a catch .

After the game, pool reporter Pat Leonard spoke with NFL V.P. of instant replay Mark Butterworth.

“The ruling on the field was an incomplete pass,” Butterworth said. “First, to overturn a call, we need clear and obvious video evidence to overturn the on-field ruling. It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds.”

Butterworth confirmed that he was referring to the fact that, when Washington hit the ground, the ball was moving in Washington’s hands.

Still, movement of the ball is permitted. Washington objectively remained in control of the ball.

And here’s the real point. Movement doesn’t prevent clear and obvious evidence that the catch was made. The question should be this: Is it clear and obvious, given that movement is permitted, that Washington made the catch?

Most would say he did. If so, the ruling on the field should have been changed from incompletion to touchdown.

sports.title: George Kittle's second TD gives 49ers 14-7 lead
sports.summary: Once again, George Kittle has made it into the end zone.
sports.body:
Kittle caught his second touchdown of the night on an 8-yard pass from Brock Purdy, putting the 49ers back ahead 14-7 with 14:13 left in the second quarter.

It took San Francisco just five plays to go 67 yards and score.

The big play on the drive came on second-and-10 from the Minnesota 48, with Purdy beating a blitz to fire a strike down the middle to Mike Evans for a 34-yard gain.

After a Christian McCaffrey 6-yard run, Purdy connected with Kittle for the tight end’s seventh touchdown of the season.

Notably, Kittle has now passed Terrell Owens to become No. 2 all-time in 49ers franchise history in receiving yards. Only Jerry Rice has more receiving yards than Kittle, as the star tight end continues to thrive in his long career.

sports.summary: The Vikings have tied things up in Mexico City.
sports.body:
Running back Aaron Jones powered his way into the end zone for a an 11-yard touchdown, knotting things up at 7-7 with 1:13 left in the first quarter.

Starting with the ball at their own 10-yard line, the Vikings were able to move into 49ers territory with a 29-yard pass from Kirk Cousins to Justin Jefferson.

Cousins then converted third-and-3 with a 16-yard pass to T.J. Hockenson to put Minnesota on the 24-yard line.

The Vikings got some help from a questionable roughing the passer call against Nick Bosa, moving the ball half the distance to the goal.

A play later, Jones bulldozed his way into the end zone for his fourth rushing touchdown of the season.

sports.title: DK Metcalf's 2025 suspension can be factor in discipline for Sunday's ejection
sports.summary: Steelers receiver DK Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
sports.body:
The disqualification, per the league, was automatic. It resulted from a pair of fouls for unsportsmanlike conduct.

The official Game Book described the first penalty as “unnecessary roughness.” Regardless, the ejection was automatic.

The next step won’t be. The league office will review the situation on Monday, with a decision inevitably made on whether additional discipline will be imposed.

And Metcalf’s history becomes relevant to the evaluation. As one source explained it, Metcalf’s two-game suspension from 2025 after an altercation with a fan in Detroit can be taken into account.

Which raises the question of whether Metcalf will be suspended again.

If it’s going to happen, it will need to happen quickly. The Broncos play the Steelers on Friday.

sports.title: Liam Coen: Everything said kick FG late in fourth, going for it a "hope play"
sports.summary: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen opted to kick a field goal from the 9-yard-line and cut the Giants' lead to 23-18 with just over three minutes to play in Sunday's game, but hopes of winning the game with a touchdown went up in smoke when the Giants picked up two first downs and ran out the clock.
sports.body:
Coen was asked about the decision to kick rather than try for the touchdown in that situation.

“We talked about it a few times,” Coen said. “Our defense — they hadn’t done anything up until that point. Everything about the charts and everything talked about it said kick the field goal, get within five points. Go get a stop and you feel pretty good about where you’re at. Just executing that down-and-distance on a fourth down is kinda challenging. They’re zero blitzing you every play, the ball’s gonna come out. It’s like a hope play.”

The Giants had gone four straight drives without picking up a first down, so some would argue in favor of the hope play while using the same argument about getting a stop in the event you score and don’t get the two-point conversion or fail to convert. The defensive stop would have remained crucial if the Jaguars had tied the game and the failure to get one at the biggest moment of the game left the Jaguars with their third loss of the season.

sports.title: Joe Brady: We can't focus on result, there's a lot to clean up
sports.summary: The Bills won again on Sunday, but head coach Joe Brady didn't sound enthused about the way they played against the Dolphins.
sports.body:
Brady’s team didn’t allow a touchdown for the third straight game and they picked up 405 yards of offense without playing from behind at all in the 26-9 win. The effort also included a pair of interceptions, a missed field goal and penalties that led the team to miss out on opportunities for touchdowns, which is likely part of what Brady will focus on in the coming days.

“I know as the head football coach, I always have to find ways for us to improve and get us to where we want to get to ,” Brady said, via Nick Suss of ESPN.com. “If we just focus on the result, we lose sight of all of those things. There’s a lot for us to clean up. We’ve got to do it in a short time because we’ve got a short turnaround.”

The Bills host the Chiefs on Sunday night in a game that has significant playoff implications in the AFC, so it’s no surprise that Brady wants the team’s attention on a cleaner effort a few days from now.

sports.title: Brock Purdy caps first drive with TD pass to George Kittle, 49ers lead 7-0
sports.summary: Much was made about the matchup between 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan and Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in advance of Sunday night's matchup between San Francisco and Minnesota.
sports.body:
Quarterback Brock Purdy capped San Francisco’s first possession with a 17-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle, giving the 49ers an early 7-0 lead.

It took the 49ers just seven plays to get down the field, with the club needing to convert just one third down. Purdy connected with Mike Evans on third-and-1 for a 14-yard gain to move the chains.

sports.title: Liam Coen: I was told ball switched hands on Parker Washington catch
sports.summary: The Giants held off the Jaguars on Sunday, but the outcome might have been different if referees had made a different ruling on a pass to Jaguars wideout Parker Washington early in the fourth quarter.
sports.body:
Washington appeared to make a diving catch in the back corner of the end zone, but officials on the field ruled that the pass was incomplete. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen challenged that Washington had control of the ball while inbounds, but the call was upheld on review.

After the game, Coen was asked if he received an explanation for the ruling by officials.

During the CBS broadcast of the game, officiating analyst Gene Steratore said that he spoke to the league office and that “they felt like there was not enough clear and obvious evidence to change the ruling on the field.”

Washington bobbled the ball briefly at first contact, but appeared to have established control by the time he hit the ground and maintained it after landing. The call went the other way in a consequential moment for the Jaguars, but an ill-timed turnover and Coen’s decisions later in the game also had a heavy hand in the final result at MetLife Stadium.

sports.title: Giants earn their most impressive win of the season with upset of Jaguars
sports.summary: The NFC East leaders surprised the AFC South leaders today.
sports.body:
In a game that few expected the Giants to win, New York took a 10-3 first quarter lead and never relinquished it, turning in an impressive performance and beating the Jaguars 23-18.

The Giants were aided by two highly controversial touchdown calls: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston got a fourth-and-goal tush push touchdown despite his helmet appearing to be down before the ball crossed the goal line, and Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington was denied a touchdown catch despite appearing to have possession with his feet down in bounds.

But the two controversies shouldn’t overshadow that this Giants team is far better than anyone expected. They’re 6-3-1 and in total control of the NFC East, and today they earned their most impressive win yet.

The Jaguars fall to 7-3, and despite the loss they’re still the overwhelming favorites to win the AFC South. This loss will hurt in the AFC playoff seeding, however, as they’re now long shots to earn the No. 1 seed.

Both the Giants and the Jaguars look like playoff teams. This was a hard-fought game between two opponents that expect to still be playing well into January. And maybe February.

sports.title: Broncos move to 8-2 with 38-24 victory over Raiders
sports.summary: A pick-six off of Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter sealed Denver's win.
sports.body:
A pick-six off of Fernando Mendoza late in the fourth quarter sealed the Broncos’ 38-24 victory.

The Raiders got down 17-0 early but came back to tie the game up at 17-17 midway through the third quarter. The Broncos responded by ripping off a pair of touchdowns, one of which came off a turnover on downs in Denver territory when Mendoza’s pass on fourth-and-2 fell incomplete.

But Las Vegas wasn’t done, scoring on a 7-yard pass from Mendoza with 4:29 left in the contest. Then the defense got a stop, setting up a potential game-tying drive just before the two-minute warning.

However, after that short break, Mendoza was looking for Tre Tucker when his pass was instead picked off by Ja’Quan McMillan — who returned it for a game-sealing, 35-yard pick-six.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix finished the contest 19-of-35 for 225 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Evan Engram led with 74 yards on six catches. Running back Jonah Coleman had 111 yards on 24 carries plus four catches for 18 yards.

On the other side, Mendoza finished 18-of-37 for 267 yards with three touchdowns and one pick in his second start. He was sacked five times. His first touchdown pass went to Ashton Jeanty, who had 90 yards on five catches to go along with 79 yards on 11 carries. His 46-yard run was his longest of the season.

With the win, the Broncos move to 8-2. They’ll have a short week, as they’ll face the Steelers on the road for next week’s Black Friday game.

The Raiders fall to 4-7. They’ll be on the road again next week in primetime, with the matchup against the Browns flexed to Sunday Night Football.

sports.title: Robert Saleh: We played disgusting football on Sunday
sports.summary: The Titans were on the receiving end of a thrashing in Dallas on Sunday.
sports.body:
The Cowboys scored touchdowns on seven of their eight possessions and racked up 480 yards before kneeling out at the end of a 51-30 win. Their offense settled for three field goals in the first half and couldn’t keep up with the stream of points that the Cowboys generated over the course of the afternoon.

After the game, Titans head coach Robert Saleh said that his team “took a step back today.”

“There’s a lot of things that need to change,” Saleh said, via the team’s website. “Obviously, it’s disgusting football, it’s embarrassing football. And obviously that starts with me.”

Saleh’s frustration with Sunday’s performance is evident, but the performance wasn’t totally out of left field. It was the third straight game that the Titans allowed at least 40 points and at least 459 yards, so the defensive issues were already apparent before the Cowboys full exploited them.

sports.title: Officials deny Jaguars TD on sensational catch by Parker Washington
sports.summary: Washington appeared to make a superb touchdown catch, but the officials and the replay office ruled it incomplete.
sports.body:
The officials ruled it incomplete, and after the Jaguars challenged, the replay review ruled that Washington did not make the catch. The ruling of incomplete pass stood, and the Jaguars settled for a field goal that cut the Giants’ lead to 20-9.

It was a highly questionable call, questioned even by former NFL referee Gene Steratore, the CBS rules analyst who said on the game broadcast that he thought it was a catch.

Washington is having a sensational season, and that was perhaps his greatest play yet — or at least it would have been, if it had been ruled a catch.

The Giants previously got a touchdown on a Jameis Winston quarterback sneak, even though replays appeared to show Winston’s helmet hit the ground before the ball crossed the goal line. Now there have been two controversial touchdown calls, both in the Giants’ favor.

sports.title: Jets beat Chargers 27-24 to end five-game losing streak
sports.summary: The Jets scored on their first five possessions and then ran out the clock on the Chargers from there.
sports.body:
Geno Smith threw three touchdown passes and the Jets scored on their first five possessions of the game. Their sixth and final possession began after the Chargers cut their lead to 27-24 on the final play before the two minute warning and the Jets were able to run for a pair of first downs that allowed them to head home with their third win of the season.

The Jets’ five scoring drives were all long marches down the field that ate up clock and cut down on the Chargers’ margin for error during their own time with the ball. The Jets were 9-of-11 on third downs over the course of the afternoon and Smith’s efficient 17-of-21 passing for 176 yards was matched by a strong rushing attack.

Breece Hall had 20 carries for 86 yards and Braelon Allen chipped in 16 carries for 75 more yards. Hall caught one of Smith’s touchdowns and veteran Sterling Shepard caught the other two after coming up as a practice squad elevation to help cover for the absences of Omar Cooper and Isaiah Williams.

The Chargers were fairly efficient as well and they avoided the turnovers that plagued them during their 0-8 start to the season, but a three-and-out to open the third quarter was followed by a 10-minute Jets scoring drive and the defense’s inability to get off the field didn’t leave the Chargers with enough opportunities to pick up their second win of the season.

They’ll remain in Los Angeles in Week 12 to host the reeling Patriots while the 3-8 Jets will be in Miami to try to avoid a season sweep at the hands of the Dolphins.

sports.title: Fernando Mendoza's second TD pass tied Raiders-Broncos at 17-17
sports.summary: The Raiders are back in business.
sports.body:
After the Broncos failed to convert on fourth-and-1 in their own territory, quarterback Fernando Mendoza connected with Ian Thomas for a game-tying, 19-yard touchdown midway through the third quarter.

Facing fourth down at their own 39-yard line, the Broncos elected to go for it with a QB sneak. But Bo Nix wasn’t pushed across the line to gain, resulting in a turnover on downs. The officials reviewed it and the call was upheld.

With great field position, Las Vegas took full advantage of the opportunity, largely with the run game. Mike Washington took four consecutive carries before Mendoza faked it to him, rolled to the right, and hit Thomas in stride down the field for his second career passing touchdown.

sports.title: Broncos lead Raiders 17-10 at halftime
sports.summary: The Broncos got out to a 17-0 lead, but the Raiders have settled in after a rough start to narrow that advantage to 17-10 at halftime.
sports.body:
Denver opened the scoring with a 38-yard field goal by Wil Lutz off of a blocked punt in Las Vegas territory. The club then scored on a 1-yard pass from quarterback Bo Nix to tight end Adam Trautman and had another 1-yard touchdown from Jonah Coleman on a run.

But after that, the Raiders came alive. First, a 46-yard run by Ashton Jeanty set up a 28-yard field goal by Matt Gay to get Las Vegas on the board. Then Jeanty came through for rookie Fernando Mendoza, catching a pass deep down the right sideline and taking it all the way for a 68-yard touchdown to narrow Denver’s lead to seven points.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills defense has spent the past several weeks keeping opponents out of the end zone. On Sunday, against the Miami Dolphins, that stretch of defensive football put the 2026 Bills in the franchise record book. Buffalo broke the record at the end of the first half, pushing it to 40 straight drives without allowing a touchdown, and added to it in the second half. Miami didn’t score a touchdown and the drive record stands at 43. The Bills haven’t allowed a touchdown in three straight games, a first for the franchise. This streak began during Buffalo’s Week 8 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, following a first-quarter touchdown run by Derrick Henry. The Bills held Baltimore without another touchdown, then kept the Minnesota Vikings and New York Jets out of the end zone entirely. Against Minnesota, Buffalo allowed just two field goals in a 23-6 Week 9 win. Last week, the Jets managed four field goals in a 31-12 loss, despite moving the ball into the red zone twice. By the time the Bills returned home to face Miami, they had gone 33 consecutive opponent drives without allowing a touchdown, the longest active streak in the NFL. It was also quite a turnaround for a defense that had struggled through the first six games of the season. Buffalo allowed an average of 28.5 points per game during that stretch, but held its next three opponents to a combined 28 points. Head coach Joe Brady credited improved communication and a better understanding of the defensive scheme for the change. And while the Bills have continued to give up yards at times, they’ve been much better at keeping those yards from turning into touchdowns. Buffalo started the game forcing punts on Miami’s first two possessions. They then allowed the Dolphins to move the ball, but eventually the Bills’ defense settled in and forced Miami to settle for a field goal. The Dolphin’s fourth drive ended in a punt before their fifth got them close enough to put three more points on the board. That stop tied the 1999 Bills’ team. sports.title: Josh Allen makes NFL history with combination of passing and rushing
sports.summary: There are plenty of ways to measure Josh Allen’s place in NFL history. Passing yards, passing touchdowns, rushing touchdowns. Pick a category, and the Buffalo Bills quarterback is probably climbing the leaderboard. But there is one particular combination of accomplishments that no player in NFL hist
sports.body: There are plenty of ways to measure Josh Allen’s place in NFL history. Passing yards, passing touchdowns, rushing touchdowns. Pick a category, and the Buffalo Bills quarterback is probably climbing the leaderboard. But there is one particular combination of accomplishments that no player in NFL history has managed to put together. Until now. Allen has officially moved into the NFL’s top 50 all-time passing yards leaders. He entered Sunday’s game needing 20 yards to pass Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner, who finished his career with 32,344 yards. Allen started the day completing two of his first three passes. The first was a 9-yard pass to DJ Moore. The second was 32-yard shot to Khalil Shakir. But, of course, he didn’t stop there. After five straight incompletions spread across two drives, Allen hit Ray Davis for a six yard completion and then found Dawson Knox across the middle for another 23. Those 70 yards had Allen leap both Warner and Cam Newton (32, 382) to land at number 49 on the NFL’s all-time list. Moving into the top 50 in passing yards did more than give Allen another name to cross off the leaderboard. It made him the first player in NFL history to rank among the top 50 in career passing yards, passing touchdowns, and rushing touchdowns. Here’s where Allen stands on each of the NFL’s all-time lists: * Passing yards: Number 49. (Next up is Ken Anderson with 32,838 yards) * Passing touchdowns: Tied at Number 38. Both Allen and Donovan McNabb have thrown 344 scoring passes. * Rushing touchdowns: Number 16 with 90. Allen’s place on the rushing touchdown list is the fun one, considering that the 15 players ahead of him are all running backs. His 90 career rushing touchdowns are already the most by a quarterback in NFL history, and he’s just one away from joining the top 12 all-time. The three-category milestone adds to a résumé that already includes an NFL MVP award (2024 NFL season), multiple Pro Bowl selections, and a collection of league and franchise records. Allen is definitely making his case for a future in Canton – all that’s missing is that Lombardi trophy.

sports.body: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. Today, for the first time in three weeks, we’re not handing out a pre-blame ball. The Jets have a plausible path to victory against the 1-8 Los Angeles Chargers, so pre-game ball it is. The pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Chargers goes to (drum roll please) - Garrett Wilson! The Chargers have a pretty good run defense. They allowed just 15 rushing yards last week against the Baltimore Ravens. They have held five of nine opponents under 120 yards rushing, and they have allowed just 3.9 rushing yards per attempt for the season. This could be a fairly difficult afternoon for the Jets’ running game. The passing game is a different story. The Chargers rank 28th in the NFL in net yards allowed per passing attempt. The Chargers also struggle to get to the quarterback, with just 15 sacks for the season. The top receivers on opposing teams have routinely excelled against the Chargers’ mediocre secondary. The loss of Derwin James at safety has badly hurt the Chargers’ secondary, and their mediocre cornerbacks have not been able to compensate. sports.body: The New York Jets activated veteran wide receiver Sterling Shepard from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is out for today’s game with an ankle injury, leaving the Jets short at wide receiver. Sterling Shepard is a 33 year old, 5’ 10”, 195 pound wide receiver. He was originally drafted out of Oklahoma by the New York Giants with the 40th overall pick in the 2nd round of the 2016 NFL draft. Shepard was an effective receiver for the Giants early in his career. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Giants before moving on after the 2023 season. Shepard played with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2024 and 2025 before being signed as an unrestricted free agent by the Jets in 2026. Sterling Shepard has been elevated to the active roster twice this season before today. He has been targeted twice by the Jets, with one reception good for three yards. The Jets needed another body at wide receiver with Cooper out. The team has Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell active, but behind those two are Tim Patrick and Malik McClain, who are unlikely to provide much value. Unfortunately, Shepard likely has little left to offer the Jets. He will turn 34 years old in February. Shepard has not exceeded 400 receiving yards in a season, a 50% success rate, or 7 yards per target since all the way back in 2020. The Jets might be better off giving practice squad receiver Jamaal Pritchett a shot. Pritchett has excelled each of the last two training camps, only to be buried on the practice squad in the regular season. Regardless of whether the Jets elevated Shepard or Pritchett, they will be thin at wide receiver until Cooper makes it back. In the meantime, who knows, maybe Shepard has a turn back the clock performance left in his tank.

sports.body: CBS has a doubleheader today while FOX will show a single game to each region. If you live in the New York area, you will see: Dolphins at Bills early on CBS Jaguars at Giants late on CBS Jets at Chargers late on FOX There are a couple of things worth noting about this game between the Jets and the Chargers. First of all, it is on FOX. While I’m sure many of you know this already, AFC games are no longer automatically shown on CBS, and NFC games are no longer automatically shown on FOX. With the Giants playing on CBS in the late timeslot, this game has to be shown on FOX. Also note that kickoff time is scheduled for 4:05 pm Eastern Time. Many late games kick off at 4:25, but this one is scheduled 20 minutes earlier at 4:05. Adam Amin and Drew Brees will be on the call for FOX. Given the quality of the teams and FOX only showing a single game on this Sunday, you might imagine this game will not have a wide distribution. FOX affiliates based in cities in New York State and Southern California will show the game. So will the FOX affiliates in Hartford, Pittsburgh, and Kansas City. To see whether Jets vs. Chargers will be shown in your area along with the other Week 11 action, go to 506sports.com. If this game is shown by your local FOX affiliate, you can stream it on FoxOne and NFL+. If the game is not shown by your local FOX affiliate, you can stream it on NFL Sunday Ticket through YouTube and YouTube TV. Separate subscriptions are required for all of these options.
